claims.statement: Termind is organized around shared Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Remote Infrastructure, Persistence, and Presentation frameworks, while TFM and TFI own native UI, platform adapters, and lifecycle; shared modules must not depend on an app target.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests apply distinct exact import checks rather than blanket prohibitions: Domain excludes its specified UI/storage/security/network/commerce/SSH/terminal imports; shared Application additionally excludes TermindInfrastructure, TermindPersistence and SwiftData, and Persistence excludes Infrastructure and Remote Infrastructure. The five non-presentation frameworks exclude app targets and specified native UI/system imports, while Presentation has its own rule excluding app targets, UIKit, AppKit, storage, Infrastructure, Remote Infrastructure and StoreKit but permitting SwiftUI.

Persistence exclusively owns SwiftData models, historical schemas, migrations and the shared container factory, using TermindSchemaV59 and TermindMigrationPlan with automatic CloudKit disabled. Lightweight stages extend from V38 through V59; V55/V56 replace Host for terminal transports and Wake-on-LAN, V57 adds themes and appearance selections, V58 adds Host creation ordering without inventing historical dates, and V59 adds optional remote MCP implementation descriptions. Local schema migrations do not change independently versioned CloudKit envelopes.

Platform composition roots select storage and retain the shared factory's containers rather than define schemas; desktop alerts and exits on second-instance or store-lock contention and fatalErrors on other database startup errors, while mobile presents unavailable data on composition failure.

AgentKit is separately versioned and consumed as a remote Swift Package rather than sibling or maintenance working-tree edits. AgentKit owns host-neutral runtime responsibilities while Termind registers its host-specific SSH/SFTP tools through TermindAgentTools.
AgentKit owns the host-neutral agent loop, approval gate, provider adapters, MCP client, and built-in tools; Termind must not add Termind-specific SSH, SFTP, UI, or host behavior to it.

Termind registers host-aware agent functionality additively through TermindAgentTools, whose injected environment supplies host, connection, authentication, metrics, background-command, and scratch services; AssistantToolRegistry supplies AgentKit built-ins and then these additional tools.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests guard AgentKit runtime type redefinition, ListViewKit allowlisting, authentication ownership and benchmark independence, and enforce engine-registry and multiplexer-dialect isolation: selected shared and feature roots cannot reference listed implementations, while transport facades cannot bypass engine registration or startup preparation.

Connection-history ownership is layered and independent from device naming: Domain defines events that reference sourceDeviceID, Application defines the history model/repository port, and Persistence owns event storage/journal transactions; the reusable DeviceRecord-to-name directory has its own Domain value, Application model/port, and Persistence repository, while TFM supplies trimmed kern.hostname with a DeviceKit fallback and TFI supplies DeviceKit's Device.current.safeDescription directly as their app-owned naming adapters.

The actual shared-framework Xcode target graph is consumer-to-dependency: Presentation depends on Application and Domain; Remote Infrastructure on Infrastructure, Application and Domain; Infrastructure on Persistence, Application and Domain; Persistence on Application and Domain; Application on Domain. Both apps depend on all six frameworks.

Mobile composition accepts an injected container for testing, otherwise chooses a file-backed Application Support store for live operation or an in-memory store for tests and injected hosts; it constructs the shared Persistence container rather than the schema.

The architecture tests' @Model guard only scans the desktop and mobile app roots plus Domain, Application, and Infrastructure; import scans are exact import-line checks and concrete-symbol checks only look for a fixed list, so tests do not prove all intended ownership boundaries exhaustively.

AgentKit's remote requirement is upToNextMinorVersion from 4.0.0 and the lockfile pins 4.0.0 at 3481866cd47e83f6bf56b80c432c7824f61130b9. AgentKit, libssh2-spm and libtailscale-spm are remote dependencies, not Termind submodules; .gitmodules contains only the website/assets submodule. Current AgentKit, libssh2 and Ghostty project requirements use upToNextMinorVersion; requirements and resolved pins govern consumption rather than external working-tree edits.

Desktop Application rejects its specified UI/storage/transport imports and desktop Features rejects specified storage/transport imports; mobile Application rejects SwiftUI, UIKit, SwiftData, GRDB and TermindPersistence while mobile UI rejects SwiftData, GRDB, TermindPersistence and TermindRemoteInfrastructure. Selected concrete-symbol checks apply to shared Application, desktop Application/Features and mobile Features, not mobile Application/UI.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests separately reject SwiftData repository declarations outside Persistence across apps, shared frameworks including Remote Infrastructure and Presentation, bridge, benchmark, widget and workspace-activity support; a declaration parser distinguishes definitions from mere references and requires a repository declaration in Persistence.

Desktop AppDependencies groups injected repository, remote connection, synchronization, logging, and optional shutdown services and offers in-memory host dependencies for tests; mobile live dependencies share a logged RemoteConnectionCoordinator across workspace and metrics services, whereas testing dependencies default to in-memory storage and replaceable services.

DeviceDirectoryModel registers the local installation through its directory port at initialization and resolves ID-to-name from a cached snapshot, falling back to the supplied local name for the current device; failed reload clears the snapshot, reports storageError, and increments revision, while successful explicit rename updates the local name and reloads and a failed rename retains the previous local name.

The SwiftData device-directory adapter avoids resurrecting a remotely deleted device at launch registration; explicit upsert writes only changed or new records in a committed History-journal snapshot and invokes the device-sync change callback only for nonempty mutations.

Persistence's V39 schema adds assistant model selection, and V40 removes retired per-category quarantine tables while retaining scoped quarantine; the migration plan includes lightweight V38-to-V39 and V39-to-V40 stages.
DeviceDirectoryModel defaults to an in-memory repository when no directory port is injected, and a failed initial registration does not prevent reading and displaying previously stored device names.

The device-directory regression tests verify rendering reads do not re-fetch or publish changes and that reload recovers from read failure; desktop connection-history tests verify that stable device IDs allow a rename to change the displayed name of existing events.
MobileAppModel creates the Application Support directory for live storage and prepares host, settings, metrics and history persistence before dependent feature composition.

V41 adds shared notification preferences and V42 adds agent-message provenance, chat creation relations, and durable collaboration delivery receipts without changing historical model shapes; both transitions are lightweight migration stages.

AssistantToolRegistry returns an empty registry for models without tool-call ability; otherwise it supplies a shared application scratch workspace to built-in and Termind tools, passes the conversation ID as the Termind environment scope, records plans through the event channel, and passes usable MCP servers with resolved credentials and the authorization client into AgentKit's built-in configuration rather than separately routing task updates.

TermindAgentTools combines AgentKit built-in and Termind tool presenters for persisted cards; descriptor lookup rejects MCP and requires an explicit registered presenter ID, with no legacy tool-name fallback or separate ssh_exec/ssh_wait registrations.

On macOS, the Persistence container factory acquires a nonblocking exclusive lock on the canonical disk-store URL before opening or migrating; same-process containers share the lease and retain it for container lifetime, while in-memory containers do not take it. A competing process gets PersistentStoreAccessError.inUse and closing the last container releases the lease without unlinking the lock file.
SSH execution receives the injected AgentSSHAuthenticationRegistry; Termind handles host login rather than obtaining SSH credentials via the built-in user-secret tool.

Desktop startup checks for other running copies of the same bundle before opening a live database to protect against older releases that lack the store lock; lock contention and second-instance detection present an alert and exit instead of opening the database.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests prohibit StoreKit imports specifically in TermindInfrastructure/Commerce, where RevenueCat-backed services implement commerce, rather than forbidding StoreKit throughout Infrastructure; Domain, shared Application and Presentation separately prohibit RevenueCat and RevenueCatUI imports.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests exclude FirebaseCore, FirebaseCrashlytics and FirebaseAnalytics imports in Domain, Application, Presentation and Persistence, and require the desktop and mobile plists to disable Crashlytics and general data collection by default and deactivate analytics; this does not ban the SDK in Infrastructure or Remote Infrastructure.

Beyond module imports and storage declarations, the architecture suite checks selected forwarding/mobile auth and additional connection ownership, shared CloudKit sync gates, AppStrings and dialog localization, AgentKit type names, ListViewKit import allowlisting and benchmark independence; these are targeted source assertions rather than a complete proof of every convention.
The embedded-Tailscale architecture test rejects TailscaleKit and CTailscale imports in shared Domain, Application, Presentation, and Persistence, but does not scan Infrastructure or the app roots.

Application's TerminalFindController owns logical search policy through injected actions/focus: changed queries and presented nonempty navigation are fenced during resize suspension, dismissal retains query and may suppress focus restoration, and resume only restarts the latest still-presented nonempty query.

Mobile workspace composition injects terminal action/focus callbacks into TerminalFindController; its search modifier binds SSH, Mosh, Eternal Terminal and Telnet to shared Find policy, submits previous navigation and dismisses without terminal focus restoration, while SFTP binds to the channel query.

MobileToolbarSearch owns UIKit search presentation through bindings and a submit callback rather than transport or persistence dependencies; it installs a UISearchController on the navigation owner, defers synchronization from SwiftUI updates, suppresses synchronization and input callbacks during dismissal, and removes its controller and restores presentation context when disconnected.

TerminalFindControllerTests verify retained-query restart, queryless navigation, default focus restoration, and idempotent native dismissal without focus; MobileShortcutTests verify F3 direction and Escape routing through the shared controller, rather than exercising every UIKit search-controller transition.
AssistantToolRegistry passes optional chat-model, chat-coordination and chat-source ports to AgentKit's built-in configuration while registering TermindAgentTools separately as additional tools.

TermindAgentTools omits executable list_panes and read_pane definitions when AgentPaneAccess is absent and omits host-facing scratch pull/push definitions without a workspace; its persisted-card presenter registry is constructed independently of that optional executable availability.

MobileSceneModel injects app-provided pane access into its assistant scene model; the mobile app adapter lists connected terminal workspaces with readable viewports, distinguishes closed, disconnected and missing-surface reads, and derives active/current pane metadata from scene and session ownership.

TermindAgentTools declares separate acting and planning registrations for SSH run/stdin tools, while SFTP mutations and scratch push are acting-only registrations; execution-mode availability is owned by the remote tool catalog rather than native UI.

Both app dependency roots decorate TermindAgentTools.presenterRegistry with SSHExecToolPresentation and resolve trusted descriptors before selecting the decorated presenter by ID. The decorator localizes selected SSH results while preserving IDs, layout and operation policy, delegating argument rendering to the original with generic fallback when absent; Presentation does not import Remote Infrastructure.

AgentToolPresentation is a generic renderer driven by injected profiles and vocabulary without modifying execution, approval or replay payloads. TermindToolPresentationProfiles composes knowledge, SSH, pane and chat policy, selecting an empty profile for MCP first, local pane/chat privacy by name next, and otherwise a profile by explicit presenter ID or an empty profile. Unknown or absent IDs do not recover SSH semantics by tool name, although generic descriptor metadata still drives rendering.

Profile detail distinguishes hidden output from default fallback, stopping hidden content before generic JSON/error rendering; local pane/chat privacy applies independently of presenter availability or executable registration. Trusted app composition gates descriptor presenter lookup through TermindAgentTools, which rejects MCP metadata selecting local code. MCP receives an empty profile, not raw-JSON preservation: default decoded results use generic items without a presenter, or an explicitly caller-supplied presenter and its layout; non-JSON results use generic text/error rendering.

AgentToolPresentationProfileTests verifies injected phase/detail/approval/truncation policy and custom vocabulary, registered-ID profile selection across a tool rename and no name recovery for unknown or absent IDs. Its MCP regression verifies rejection of a local SSH presenter ID from remote metadata, generic Value-field fallback, and explicitly supplied Projected-field presentation with caller-supplied layout.
